You are exploring the Go codebase at /bench/repo (the "memos" project). Answer these three questions with exact file paths and line numbers (path:line). Be very thorough; verify by reading the actual code.

Q1: Something in the server keeps links to externally-stored attachment content (e.g. S3 presigned URLs) from going stale. Identify: the component (type/function name), the schedule/interval it runs at (cite the constant/line), and where it is wired into server startup (the exact call site path:line, e.g. in internal/server/server.go or a runner registration).

Q2: The server can notify external systems over HTTP when content changes (webhooks). Find: (a) the function where the outbound HTTP delivery actually executes (the http.Post/client.Do call) with path:line; (b) what protects it from SSRF / being pointed at internal network addresses (e.g. a URL validator, dial control, httpgetter package restrictions) with path:line. Check internal/webhook and internal/httpgetter and anything else relevant. If there is NO SSRF protection on the webhook path specifically, say so explicitly and show what you checked.

Q3: Users can authenticate through third-party identity providers. Which package defines the provider abstraction (interface / factory), and which concrete protocol implementation package ships (e.g. OAuth2, OIDC)? Give package paths and key files with line numbers for the interface and the concrete implementation.

Report findings as structured facts with citations, no prose padding.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. ## Q1: Presigned URL refresher for external attachment storage

- **Component**: `s3presign.Runner` — type at `/bench/repo/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:16`; core logic `Runner.CheckAndPresign` at `/bench/repo/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:47`; loop `Runner.Run` at `runner.go:29`.
- **Schedule**: every 12 hours — `const runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12` at `/bench/repo/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27` (comment at line 26). Refresh criterion: re-presigns when the URL is no longer valid for the next 4 days (expiry is 5 days), `runner.go:85-91`; new presigned URL stored as attachment `Reference` at `runner.go:108-119`.
- **Startup wiring**: `Server.startBackgroundRunners` at `/bench/repo/server/server.go:153`, called from `server.go:129`. Runner constructed at `server.go:162` (`s3presign.NewRunner(s.Store)`), immediate pass `RunOnce(ctx)` at `server.go:163`, continuous goroutine `s3presignRunner.Run(s3Context)` at `server.go:169`.

## Q2: Webhook HTTP delivery and SSRF protection

**(a) Outbound delivery execution**
- `webhook.Post` in `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:120`; the actual HTTP send is `resp, err := safeClient.Do(req)` at `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:152` (request built at line 126). Async path: `PostAsync` at `webhook.go:184` enqueues to worker goroutines (`webhook.go:42-55`) which call `Post`. Triggered from `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:43` and `:71`.

**(b) SSRF protection — it exists, in two layers, both in `internal/webhook`:**
1. **Dial-time guard (defeats DNS rebinding)**: `safeClient` at `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:32-37` uses a Transport with `DialContext: safeDialContext`; `safeDialContext` at `webhook.go:59-77` resolves the host and rejects any IP in a reserved/private range (`isReservedIP` check at `webhook.go:71-73`).
2. **Create/update-time URL validation**: `webhook.ValidateURL` at `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go:62` — enforces absolute URL, http/https scheme (`validate.go:67`), and no resolution to reserved IPs (`validate.go:71-81`). Blocked ranges in `reservedCIDRs` at `validate.go:14-23` (loopback, RFC-1918, link-local/IMDS 169.254.0.0/16, IPv6 ::1, fc00::/7, fe80::/10). `isReservedIP` at `validate.go:44`; escape hatch `var AllowPrivateIPs bool` at `validate.go:41` (default false; only set in tests). Called from `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go:74`, `:161`, `:182`.

- `internal/httpgetter` is a separate concern (link-preview metadata fetching, not webhooks); it has its own guard `ErrInternalIP` at `/bench/repo/internal/httpgetter/html_meta.go:18` with checks at `html_meta.go:76`, `:93`, `:124` — though `/bench/repo/internal/httpgetter/image.go:21` uses a plain `http.Get`. Not on the webhook path.

## Q3: Third-party identity provider packages

- **Abstraction package**: `github.com/usememos/memos/internal/idp` — `/bench/repo/internal/idp/idp.go`. Note: there is **no Go interface**; the abstraction is the shared result type `IdentityProviderUserInfo` struct at `/bench/repo/internal/idp/idp.go:3-8`. Provider selection is a type switch on the stored config, not a factory in `idp`: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go:120` (`if identityProvider.Type == storepb.IdentityProvider_OAUTH2`).
- **Concrete implementation shipped**: OAuth2 only — package `github.com/usememos/memos/internal/idp/oauth2`, `/bench/repo/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go`:
  - `IdentityProvider` struct at `oauth2.go:20`
  - Constructor/factory `NewIdentityProvider(config *storepb.OAuth2Config)` at `oauth2.go:27`
  - `ExchangeToken` (with PKCE support) at `oauth2.go:47`
  - `UserInfo` at `oauth2.go:83`
- **Wiring**: `resolveSSOIdentity` at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go:104` instantiates via `oauth2.NewIdentityProvider(...)` at `auth_service_sso.go:121`, then `ExchangeToken` (`:126`) and `UserInfo` (`:130`). No OIDC/LDAP/SAML implementation exists under `internal/idp` (only the `oauth2` subdirectory).
